accepted_review_findings:
[reviewer finding R1, moderate] The public research question (assets/task.md lines 5-17 and the identical LIT-F01-topic statement) is not just a problem area: its five sub-areas reproduce the target paper's own framing item by item, and the example lists name the target's solution classes. Area 1 makes 'what each costs per state update' a survey axis and lists 'spatially structured reservoirs' (the target's contribution (a) is a spatially local reservoir that lowers per-step cost). Area 2 couples memory capacity with a stability trade-off and lists 'delay-based memory extensions' (the target's second stated limitation and contribution (b)). Area 3 lists NLMS, which the target paper itself calls a 'minimalist baseline' it chose for evaluation-time readout adaptation (contribution (c)), not a standard ESN readout method. The private rubric (section 4) lists four reference gaps that correspond one-to-one to these areas, and section 2 J5 expects the library to contain little or nothing on NLMS, delay-based memory or small-world reservoirs. That expectation shows these items are in the question because of the target, not because of the library. No single phrase names the method, and the combination is never stated as a gap. Even so, the question steers the solver toward the target's gap axes and solution families. The constructor itself asked for an independent neutrality check (unresolved_blockers[3]).
Required repair: Restate the research question as problem areas without target-specific example lists. For example: (1) reservoir topology and computational cost of reservoir models; (2) memory capacity and dynamical stability of reservoirs; (3) training of the readout, offline and online; (4) hyperparameter optimisation of reservoirs; (5) how reservoir models compare with gradient-trained forecasting models on standard benchmarks. Drop 'what each costs per state update', 'spatially structured', 'delay-based memory extensions' and the explicit 'NLMS' item, or replace them with generic wording. Apply the change identically in task.md, LIT-F01-topic and any rubric references, and update hashes. The binding LIT scope prescribes the current wording, so the adjudicator must explicitly confirm or override that scope wording. This round may be the last allowed repair round; if so, record the outcome rather than silently passing.

[reviewer finding R2, minor] The public LIT-F01-topic statement says 'the cited library abstracts only show that these areas are represented in the background literature'. The five cited abstracts support area 1 (bg005 structured/permutation topologies; bg009 topologies), memory capacity in area 2 (bg009), area 4 (bg018 CMA-ES) and area 5 (bg023 linear vs Transformer; bg022 MLP mixing). None of them covers area 3 (readout training / online adaptation), the stability / edge-of-chaos or delay parts of area 2, or per-update cost. The package's own unresolved_blockers[6] states that no supplied background source covers the memory/delay or online-readout areas, which contradicts the public parenthetical.
Required repair: Either narrow the parenthetical to the areas the cited abstracts actually support (topology, memory-capacity tasks, CMA-ES tuning, comparisons with Transformer/linear/MLP forecasters), or drop the parenthetical from the public statement and keep the evidence-coverage note private. Make sure the public statement does not contradict unresolved_blockers.

[reviewer finding R3, minor] The public contract asks only for honest coverage limitations ('whether the coverage limitations are honest'; area coverage rule). The library is a shared controller library whose composition is explicitly unverified (LIT-U01; rubric section 5). If the served library does hold FORCE/BPDC/small-world/delay works, J5 as written could lead a judge to expect a 'thin evidence' limitation in areas where an honest solver found and cited real evidence. That would be a hidden expectation that is not in the public contract.
Required repair: Make J5 conditional on the library actually served: credit limitations that match what the served library holds, and penalise only fabricated support or claimed absences contradicted by the library. Keep the current list only as a constructor observation about the inspected sources.
controller_notes: [controller note, rule R4] Rewrite the public research question and the LIT-F01-topic statement so that they describe the problem area only. The five sub-areas currently reproduce the target paper's own framing item by item; replace them with standard areas any literature review of this problem area would cover, or with fewer, broader areas, so that no list mirrors the target's ingredient list, motivating limitations, or benchmarking objective. Do not mention in any public text, even negatively, what is withheld.
